stories.title: Chintu the Curious Squirrel
body: In a big banyan tree lived a little squirrel named Chintu. Chintu loved to ask questions. "Why is the sky blue? Why do birds sing? Why is honey sweet?" he asked all day long.
One morning, Chintu saw a line of tiny ants carrying crumbs much bigger than themselves. "How can such small ants carry such big food?" he wondered. So he decided to follow them.
The ants marched over stones, under leaves, and across a little stream on a floating twig. Chintu watched carefully. Every ant helped the other. When one ant was tired, two ants took its load.

"Now I understand!" said Chintu happily. "They are not strong because they are big. They are strong because they help each other!" From that day, Chintu helped his squirrel friends collect nuts together, and their work became easy and fun.
Chintu learned that curiosity is a gift, and teamwork makes even the hardest work light.

stories.title: The Elephant Who Was Afraid of Mice
body: Gajraj was the biggest elephant in the whole forest. He had huge legs, long tusks, and a trumpet so loud it could be heard for miles. Every animal respected him — except for one tiny problem. Gajraj was terribly afraid of mice!
One day, a little mouse named Munni got stuck under a fallen branch. "Help! Help!" she squeaked. All the animals heard, but the branch was too heavy for them to lift.

Gajraj came near. His heart was pounding. "A mouse! I am so scared," he whispered. But Munni's cries were so sad that Gajraj forgot his fear for a moment. He gently lifted the heavy branch with his strong trunk.

"Thank you, big friend!" said Munni, hugging his foot. "You are not just strong, you are brave and kind." Gajraj smiled. He realized that being scared is normal, but helping someone in need makes us braver than our fears.
After that day, Gajraj and Munni became the best of friends, and Gajraj was never afraid of mice again.

stories.title: Raju the Honest Rabbit
body: Raju the rabbit was hopping through the meadow when he found a shiny golden carrot lying on the path. It was the most beautiful carrot he had ever seen!
"Whose carrot is this?" Raju wondered. He could have eaten it quickly, but he knew it belonged to someone. So he picked it up and hopped from door to door, asking, "Did you lose a golden carrot?"
Finally, he reached the home of old Grandma Tortoise, who was crying. "I lost my special golden carrot! My grandchild gave it to me," she sobbed. Raju happily returned it.
Grandma Tortoise was so pleased that she gave Raju a whole basket of fresh carrots. "Honesty is the sweetest treasure of all," she said with a smile.
Raju hopped home with his basket, feeling happier than he had ever felt — not because of the carrots, but because he had done the right thing.

stories.title: The Peacock and the Rain
body: Moti the peacock had the most beautiful feathers in the jungle — blue, green, and gold, shining like jewels. But Moti was very proud. He laughed at the plain brown sparrow and the little grey mouse.
"Look at me! I am the most beautiful," he would say, spreading his feathers. The other animals felt sad, but Moti did not care.
One summer, there was no rain for many days. The rivers dried up and everyone was thirsty. The wise old owl said, "Only the one who dances with a pure heart can call the rain clouds."

Moti danced beautifully, but no rain came. Then the plain brown sparrow began to sing a gentle song, thinking not of herself but of her thirsty friends. Slowly, dark clouds gathered, and the rain poured down!

Moti understood at last. "Beauty on the outside means nothing without kindness inside," he said. He apologized to everyone, and from that day, Moti used his lovely dance to make his friends happy, not to boast.

quiz.q: What problem came to the jungle?
